provenanceNote: Eleven digits failing Norway's modulus-11 check: the correct check digits for 131086335 are 27, so this ends 28 and no bearer can exist. Asked as Swedish deliberately — naming a country does not make the recognition less true, and 'you have the wrong country' is the answer a caller who guessed wrong needs.

The same digits with no issuedBy, which is the detect() path. Pins the half of the decision the named-country fixture cannot reach: Plan 2 established that a multi-country consultation reports the generic reason, and a recognition is the exception to that, because 'this is a Norwegian number' is an answer to 'what is this?' where 'Sweden says the check digit is wrong' is not.

Day 31 of month 13, so no bearer can exist for two independent reasons: the date cannot occur and the check digits are wrong (311399123 requires 09, this ends 00). It pins that recognition is shape-only — a value is reported as Norwegian without its date being validated, which is exactly what a recognize-only tier should do and exactly what would be wrong if the country were ever promoted to full support.

Skatteetaten's shape is eleven digits with no separator, so a hyphenated Norwegian number is not recognized. Kept because the boundary is worth pinning in the corpus rather than trusting a reading of the pattern: it is the difference between recognizing a shape and guessing at one.

DVV documents 131052-308T as its own example, so this fixture deliberately carries U instead: the modulus-31 control character for 131052308 is T, making this code invalid and leaving it no possible bearer. The letter is also what makes the case reachable at all — before spec/characters.json learned Finland's alphabet this input returned InvalidCharacter.
Intermediate character A, which decree 690/2022 assigns to births from 1 January 2000. Control character P where the correct one for 010101123 is N, so no bearer can exist.

Intermediate character Y, one of the letters decree 690/2022 added for 1900s births so codes would not run out; DVV issued the first Y code on 19 December 2023. Control character D where the correct one for 150375246 is C, so no bearer can exist. This is the fixture that would fail if the marker set were encoded from pre-2023 memory rather than from the decree.

The same invalid code in lowercase. The normalizer deliberately does not fold case, because PHP's mb_strtoupper and JavaScript's toUpperCase do not agree for every input and a divergence between the runtimes is worse than a lowercase Finnish code being reported as InvalidCharacter. This fixture is what stops that limitation being quietly removed by someone adding a case fold without reading why it is absent.

A published MedCom test number in its display form, which is character-for-character a shape-valid Finnish code: six digits, a hyphen, three digits, a digit control character. It parses as Danish, and this fixture pins that a parse outranks a recognition — without it, nothing stops a later change reclassifying valid Danish numbers as unrecognized foreign ones. The collision is structural rather than coincidental, because modulus-11 is not a Danish validity rule, so most such Finnish codes parse as Danish.

The other side of the fixture above: the same six digits with a letter control character, which no Danish shape can match. Constructed and invalid in Finland too — the correct control character for 010490998 is 9, not T — so it has no bearer in either country. Together the two fixtures pin where the boundary between a parse and a recognition actually falls.
